get.summary:
Every provider's OAuth app credential state: the resolved client id, and for both fields whether the
value in play is a stored one or the environment's.

The setup wizard writes these once and then has no further say; until now nothing could read
back what was configured or rotate a leaked secret without editing the database by hand.

No secret is ever returned — only whether one exists and which source wins. The client
id is returned because it is a public identifier that appears in every OAuth URL a viewer's browser
already sees, and withholding it would only stop the operator checking the value most likely wrong.

put.summary:
Stores a client id and/or secret for one provider. A blank field is left untouched, so rotating a
secret needs no id and a half-filled form cannot wipe a working credential.

delete.summary:
Clears a provider's STORED credentials, handing resolution back to the environment.

Destructive, and the repair path for a real failure: a stored secret shadows the environment,
so an operator who fixes a rotated secret in their .env keeps getting 401s from a stale stored
value they cannot see. It is a separate verb precisely so it can never happen by accident.

post.summary:
Counts, WITHOUT replaying anything, exactly how many journal events a tenant + window + optional
event-type scope would re-apply to the named projection — the count an operator must see and confirm
before Task<IActionResult> AdminController.ExecuteEventReplay(AdminEventReplayExecuteRequestDto request, CancellationToken ct) is allowed to run.

Re-applies every journal event in the given scope to the named projection's real `ApplyAsync`,
in order — the same per-projection fold the live driver uses, never a second replay engine. Refused
(STALE_COUNT) unless long AdminEventReplayExecuteRequestDto.ExpectedCount matches the scope's
REAL count at execution time, so an operator can only ever act on a number they were actually shown.
`ApplyAsync` is idempotent by contract (upsert keyed on EventId), so running this twice re-applies
the same upserts rather than double-counting anything. Always audited, naming the acting operator, the
exact scope, and the count applied.

get.summary:
Start the Twitch OAuth flow. Redirects the browser to Twitch's authorization page.
Pass `redirect_uri` for mobile / desktop-loopback deep-link callbacks (e.g.
`nomnomzbot://callback`). Pass `client=web` for the served-web dashboard: a full-page redirect
can't receive a JSON token body, so the callback returns the tokens in the URL fragment + an HttpOnly
cookie instead. A RETURNING operator's re-auth is additive: when the navigation carries a live web
session cookie, the requested scope set widens to `base ∪ granted ∪ recorded-missing` so a re-grant
clears every recorded gap and never drops an already-held scope (a fresh login gets the base set).
Pass `invite` on a streamer sign-in to carry an invite code (S-INVITE-TIER): it is held in the
server-side state and redeemed once, after sign-in, on the channel the sign-in opened.

Handle the OAuth callback from Twitch. Exchanges the authorization code for platform tokens and returns
them in a JSON body (S098c: a mobile `redirect_uri` no longer carries any token in the query string
— mobile is a native client and reads its tokens from this response body like any other native caller).
The served-web flow is the only success path that still redirects, and only the short-lived access
token rides in that redirect's URL fragment. A streamer sign-in that carried an invite code redeems it
once on the channel it opened; the web fragment then adds `invite=redeemed`, or
`invite=failed&invite_reason=...`. A failed redeem never blocks the sign-in.

post.summary:
Exchange an OAuth authorization code for platform tokens (mobile / SPA flow).
The client handles the Twitch redirect directly and sends the code + redirect_uri
to this endpoint for server-side token exchange.

Redeem the `login_code` a web sign-in handed to a second listed dashboard origin (it arrives in that
page's URL fragment). The code works once and expires after 60 seconds. The request's `Origin` must be
the origin the code was issued for; a wrong origin is refused and the code is spent all the same. On
success the refresh token is set as the HttpOnly cookie on the calling origin and the access token is
returned in the body.

Begin the no-secret streamer login (Device Code Flow). Returns a short user code + the
twitch.tv/activate URL to show the operator, plus the device code the client polls with. No Twitch app
registration and no client secret — NomNomzBot's shipped public client id drives it.

Poll a streamer device login once. Until the operator approves, the status is `pending` /
`slow_down`; on `authorized` the session is opened and the response carries the platform
tokens + user, which the client establishes exactly as it would after the redirect callback.

get.summary:
The login providers this deployment offers (platform-identity §5). Public — the login screen reads it
before any auth. Each carries the handshake flows the client should run and whether it is currently
enabled (a registered descriptor whose feature flag resolves true); disabled ones are returned so the
client can show "coming soon" rather than a dead button. Twitch is always enabled.

post.summary:
Begin the no-secret device login for a provider (platform-identity §5). The literal `twitch/device`
route is the `provider=twitch` case (literal segments win in routing), so existing clients are
unaffected; this handles every other enabled provider. 404 `UNKNOWN_PROVIDER` / 403
`PROVIDER_DISABLED` gate it.

Poll a provider device login once (platform-identity §5). Delegates the Twitch case to the established
streamer-session flow (incl. the web HttpOnly-cookie custody); other enabled providers plug in with
their login seams.

get.summary:
Begin an auth-code + PKCE login for a provider (kick / twitter, platform-identity §10.3): generate the
PKCE pair, stash the verifier + provider key server-side under a single-use state nonce, and 302 the
whole page to the provider's authorize URL. 404 `UNKNOWN_PROVIDER` / 403 `PROVIDER_DISABLED` gate it.

post.summary:
Refresh an expired access token. Custody — cookie (web) vs body (native) — is decided by whether the
    request itself carries the `nnz_refresh_token` HttpOnly cookie; a caller-controlled `?client=`
    query flag is never consulted (S098c — it let any caller flip which custody path a request took). A
    cookie-borne refresh additionally requires an allowed Origin: `SameSite=Lax` alone still lets a
    top-level cross-site navigation attach the cookie, so a forged Origin/Referer is rejected outright. A
    body-borne (native) refresh carries no ambient browser credential, so it is not subject to that check.
    While an act-as session is open (the nnz_act_as cookie on web, actAsToken in the body on
native), the refresh hands back the SAME impersonated user under the same support session — the response
then carries impersonation and no refresh token, and the operator's own refresh token is left
untouched. Once that session is over the act-as cookie is cleared and the operator's own session is
refreshed instead, so the dashboard reloads as the operator.

Leave an act-as session from inside it (the Exit button while acting): closes the support session the
act-as token runs under — the same audited end, `sid` revocation and owner notice as ending it with
the operator's token — clears the act-as cookie, and hands back the OPERATOR's own session. Web gets it
through the normal HttpOnly refresh cookie; native sends its own refresh token in the body. With no
operator refresh token to resume, the session still ends and the response carries no token.

Log out the current session, revoking its refresh tokens. While acting as someone the person logging out
is the OPERATOR: the act-as session ends and the operator's own web session (the refresh cookie) is
revoked — the impersonated user's own sessions are never touched.

Log out of all the current user's sessions, revoking every refresh token they hold. While acting as
someone this is the OPERATOR's "everywhere": the act-as session ends and every session of the operator
behind the refresh cookie is revoked — never the impersonated user's.

Start the OAuth flow for the platform-shared bot account. This is a platform-level registration on top

Returns the Twitch authorize URL for the client to open — the resulting token is stored globally (no
per-channel binding). First-run setup uses the wizard's `system/setup/bot/oauth-url` instead

Reset the configured response for an event type back to its seeded default (disabled, chat_message,
no message/pipeline). The row is a fixed catalogue entry keyed by event type — this never deletes it.
A row bound to a pipeline, command or action is refused (400 `CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, naming the

get.summary:
Reads one page of the channel's journal, newest first, with the channel's head position. Filters are
optional: `eventType` and `source` match exactly, `from` and `to` bound the time the
event happened. Rows carry no payload (it can hold sealed personal data). Only the resolved channel's own
stream is read.

parameters.name: Take
parameters.description:
Rows per page. Bound from EITHER `Take` (the historical name) OR `pageSize` — the REST-
convention name every frontend caller actually sends. Before this alias, `?pageSize=100` bound to
nothing and silently fell back to 25, so every dashboard list was capped at 25 rows and the rest of the
data was invisible. Both query keys now populate the same value.

post.summary: Exports the channel's whole journal as a JSONL file download (one event envelope per line). Owner-only.

Imports a JSONL journal export into the channel's stream — idempotent (duplicates by EventId are skipped),
upcast on read, and atomic (all-or-nothing). Owner-only. Returns import/skip/upcast counts.

Replays every imported-but-not-yet-replayed event for the channel, in their original order, through the
SAME live-handler path a real Twitch event takes — so pipeline triggers, TTS-enabled commands, and reward
handling actually re-run for the imported history instead of just sitting silently in the journal. Owner-
only. Idempotent: only advances past NEW imported rows since the last replay, so calling it again after
nothing new was imported is a safe no-op. Cannot touch another channel's events — the runner reads only
this resolved tenant's own stream (event-store §3.3).

Backfills the channel's history from the legacy NoMercy bot database into the journal — reads the legacy file
READ-ONLY, maps each channel event to its current domain event, and appends idempotently (a re-run imports
nothing). Owner-only. Returns import/skip counts and the journal head before/after.

Rebuilds every tenant-scoped read-model projection (channel event log, analytics dailies, viewer profiles, …)
from the channel's journal — reset → replay from position 0. Owner-level. Run after a legacy import (or any
journal backfill) so the new facts surface in the read models. Returns the per-projection applied-event counts.

where the ban is permitted.

delete.summary: Removes the operator's opt-in for that channel; 404 when there was none.

post.summary:
Ban a list of accounts (for example a follow-bot storm) in EVERY channel the operator moderates, one batch
per channel (chat-client.md §3.5). The operator's own channel, the `AttackedChannels` and every offline
channel start banning at once; a live channel is held until its streamer, a lead moderator or an editor types
`!allow massban`, or until the stream ends. `ExcludedChannels` and channels whose owner opted out
get nothing. Each ban rides the operator's own token.

Unban a viewer — in THIS channel or across EVERY channel the operator moderates (the reversal of the network
ban, `Scope = "all_moderated"`). Both scopes return a NetworkBanResultDto; `this_channel`
is a one-row result. The `all_moderated` sweep is best-effort per channel and lifts each ban AS THE
OPERATOR (their own token), so Twitch — not us — decides where it is permitted.

The channel's trust tuning. A channel that has never edited it gets the shipped defaults with
`isPinned: false`, so the dashboard can show what is a default and what the operator chose.

put.summary:
Saves the channel's trust tuning, creating the row on first edit. Ranges are enforced
server-side — the four weights must sum to 1.0, tier ceilings must ascend, and no penalty, decay
or heat amount may be negative — so a policy that could not produce a sane score is rejected
rather than stored.

get.summary:
The shipped trust defaults (never pinned), so the editor can show "default" next to every
value and offer a reset without carrying its own copy of the numbers.

The channel's TTS source for OBS (widgets-overlays.md §1.2): get-or-creates the system
`audio` widget (the one Audio page every sound and TTS line plays out of; never a gallery
browse/install) and returns its OBS browser-source URL plus when it last reported running. A fresh
channel gets a working URL on the first call — no widget install required.

post.summary:
Fires a real test utterance through the LIVE dispatch pipeline (gate → censor → dispatch →
`TtsUtteranceDispatchedEvent` → overlay push), so the streamer can prove the OBS browser source
actually plays audio. This is NOT Task<IActionResult> TtsConfigController.TestVoice(string channelId, TtsTestRequestDto request, CancellationToken ct) — that endpoint only synthesizes bytes and
hands them back to the caller and never touches the overlay. Speaks in the channel's default voice (no
triggering viewer) and passes `ChannelEventId: null`, the same value a standalone chat-triggered
utterance uses — no `ChannelEvent` is created, so there is genuinely nothing for Replay to
correlate.
Skip the utterance currently playing on the overlay and advance to the next queued one.
Stop the current utterance and drop every queued utterance behind it.
Pause the overlay's TTS queue — the current utterance and everything behind it holds.
Resume a paused overlay TTS queue.

ActionRequiredItem.description:
One row of the dashboard's action-required inbox (S071a) — a real, already-detected condition that needs
            the streamer's attention, surfaced from an existing signal (never fabricated). string ActionRequiredItemDto.Kind is a
            stable machine key the dashboard groups/icons by (e.g. `integration_token_dead`,
            `held_chat_message`); string ActionRequiredItemDto.Severity is `critical` | `warning` | `info`.
            The row carries no prose. string ActionRequiredItemDto.TitleKey and string ActionRequiredItemDto.MessageKey are dashboard string-resource
names, and Dictionary<string, string> ActionRequiredItemDto.Parameters are the named values those strings format in (a provider key, a widget
name, a failure count). The client renders them in the viewer's language; int ActionRequiredItemDto.Count drives plurals.string ActionRequiredItemDto.DeepLinkRoute is the dashboard page address where the condition is fixed, with its tab when the page has tabs
            (integrations, people/queue, channel-points, ...).string ActionRequiredItemDto.Id is the item's stable identity (S-OWN22 T2), the key the dismiss endpoint accepts. Each
            source embeds whatever makes an old dismissal stale into the key, so a NEW occurrence surfaces again: a dead
            token is token:{connectionId}:{invalidatedAtUtcTicks}, a single held message is
            held:{queueItemGuid}, a per-user group of held messages is held-user:{sourceUserId}. Held
            messages from one user are grouped into ONE item: int ActionRequiredItemDto.Count pending holds, all of them in
            List<Guid> ActionRequiredItemDto.QueueItemIds, with string? ActionRequiredItemDto.SourceUserId/string? ActionRequiredItemDto.SourceUserName naming the sender.

AdminScheduledJob.description:
One row of the REAL background job queue — the `ScheduledPipelineTask` deferred-dispatch primitive
(a voice-swap auto-revert, a feather auto-hide, a timed reward) that a background sweeper fires when due.
This is never a fabricated parallel queue: it reads the exact rows `ScheduledPipelineExpiryService`
dispatches. string AdminScheduledJobDto.Status is the raw persisted value (pending/fired/cancelled/expired);
string AdminScheduledJobDto.DisplayState is the operator-facing label (queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled) derived
from it plus DateTime AdminScheduledJobDto.DueAt against the current clock. bool AdminScheduledJobDto.CanRetry is true only for a
genuinely failed (expired) job whose target pipeline still exists.

AdminTenantErrorBudget.description:
One tenant's error budget for the trailing 24-hour window, computed purely from real
`OutboundWebhookDelivery` outcomes (`Delivered` = success, `Failed`/`DeadLetter` = error;
`Pending` attempts are excluded — they have not resolved yet). There is no platform-wide blended figure:
one tenant's failures never count toward another's, because the entire point of a 2am tool is finding WHICH
tenant's integration is actually broken. A tenant with no resolved delivery attempts in the window is simply
absent from the page — never padded with a fabricated 0%. double? AdminTenantErrorBudgetDto.ErrorRate and
double? AdminTenantErrorBudgetDto.BudgetRemainingFraction are `null` when long AdminTenantErrorBudgetDto.Attempts is 0.
double AdminTenantErrorBudgetDto.TargetSuccessRate is a stated policy threshold (99%), not a measured quantity — the allowed
error rate it implies is the denominator double? AdminTenantErrorBudgetDto.BudgetRemainingFraction is computed against.

AdminTenantUsage.description:
One tenant's usage for its most recent metering period, computed purely from recorded rows
            (`UsageRecord` + `TtsUsageRecord`) — never a placeholder figure. DateTime AdminTenantUsageDto.PeriodStart/
            DateTime AdminTenantUsageDto.PeriodEnd state exactly which window the figures cover.
            Cost (S-ADMIN-4d) is reported ONLY for units the owner has actually priced via the PricedUnit
catalogue: each priced metric in IReadOnlyList<AdminTenantUsageMetricDto> AdminTenantUsageDto.Metrics carries its own cost, long? AdminTenantUsageDto.TtsCostMinorUnits
is the TTS character cost (or null if unpriced), IReadOnlyList<AdminTenantUsageCostDto>? AdminTenantUsageDto.TotalCostsByCurrency sums every
priced figure grouped by currency, and IReadOnlyList<string>? AdminTenantUsageDto.UnpricedUnitKeys names every unit this tenant
actually used that has no price yet — so an unpriced unit is never silently read as costing nothing.

AdminTenantUsageCost.description: One currency's worth of a tenant's total priced usage cost for the period.

AdminTenantUsageMetric.description:
One metered quantity for a tenant's usage period, straight off the real `UsageRecord` rows, joined
against the owner-authored `PricedUnit` catalogue (S-ADMIN-4d). long? AdminTenantUsageMetricDto.CostMinorUnits and
string? AdminTenantUsageMetricDto.Currency are both `null` when string AdminTenantUsageMetricDto.MetricKey has no `PricedUnit` row —
UNPRICED, never reported as a zero cost.

categories.description: Only the categories with a non-zero count; an empty list means a genuine zero.

isMinimum.description:
True when the count is a verified FLOOR rather than an exhaustive total — set when some references can
only be resolved at run time (a pipeline field whose value is a template placeholder, or a user code
script that resolves the resource through the SDK). The dashboard must then say the number is a MINIMUM
rather than implying completeness.

BlastRadius.description:
The real, counted set of things that reference a resource right now — surfaced in the delete confirmation
BEFORE the save (S-CONSEQ). int BlastRadiusDto.TotalReferences is zero exactly when nothing references the
resource; the dashboard renders that as an explicit "nothing else references this" statement, never as an
empty area. A lookup that FAILED is a `Result` failure and never reaches this type — reporting zero
for a failed check would cause exactly the loss the preview exists to prevent.

categoryKey.description: i18n resource key naming the kind of dependent that was counted.

count.description: The real number of rows counted right now. Never estimated.

sample.description:
Up to a handful of human-readable names of the counted rows, so the user recognises WHICH things break.
A shorter list than Count means the sample was truncated, never that the count is soft.

BlastRadiusCategory.description:
One counted category of a destructive action's blast radius. CategoryKey is an i18n
resource KEY, never a sentence — the language lives in the dashboard's string resources
(`strings.xml`), so the backend never ships English.

permanentAfterUtc.description: The instant the soft-deleted tenant becomes unrecoverable, computed from the server clock at preview time.

Everything the delete-channel confirmation must state BEFORE the button can be pressed — the largest blast
            radius in the product.
            Channel delete is a SOFT delete with a restore window: the tenant's rows stay on disk and every query
filter hides them, and only after DateTime ChannelDeletePreviewDto.PermanentAfterUtc does the data become unrecoverable. The
dialog states both the window and the date, because a button that looks irreversible and is not is as
dishonest as one that looks reversible and is not.

lives on (`AuthEnums.Platform`: twitch / youtube / kick), letting the dashboard tag each channel — and
each chat line / multi-watch pane — by its source. `ChatColor` is the streamer's Twitch chat color
(#RRGGBB), populated from `User.Color` when known — null until the first login after the color-sync
feature is deployed, or when the user has no color set; the dashboard uses it as the dynamic accent token
(design-system §2). `DeletedAt` and `PermanentAfter` are set only on a soft-deleted channel listed

(chat-decoration spec §4). `Urls` is scale-keyed ("1"/"2"/"3"); `Provider` is the source network.
`StaticUrls` holds the still image per scale for reduced motion; a non-animated emote repeats `Urls`.

minPermissionLevel.description:
The lowest rung that may run this command, by NAME —
`Everyone | Subscriber | Vip | Artist | Moderator | LeadModerator | Editor | Broadcaster`.

It used to be the ladder's raw integer, documented here as "0=everyone, 1=follower, 2=sub,
3=vip, 4=moderator, 5=broadcaster" — a scale the product has not used for a long time. The real rungs
are 0/2/4/6/10/20/30/40 and include Artist, LeadModerator and Editor, so anyone integrating against
that comment sent 5 for "broadcaster" and quietly got a command every subscriber could run.

(`$.foo.bar` syntax) found in it, capped so a huge/deeply-nested document can't flood the picker.

DangerTier.description: The danger tier of a capability — guards how low its floor may be set / whether it may be permit-granted.

DashboardChatMessage.description:
Rich chat message DTO sent to dashboard/overlay clients via SignalR. Includes structured fragments for
inline emote, mention, and cheermote rendering; field names match the frontend ChatMessagePayload type
exactly. `Message` is the raw plain-text fallback for clients that don't render fragments;
`Fragments` are the structured text/emote/cheermote/mention pieces; `UserType` is the derived
role (broadcaster | moderator | vip | subscriber | viewer); `Color` is the user's chat color
(#RRGGBB); `MessageType` is text | channel_points_highlighted | channel_points_sub_only | user_intro;
`AvatarUrl` and `Pronouns` are additive hub-broadcast-layer enrichment (`IHubUserEnricher`),
null when unavailable.

viewerCount.description: Last known viewer count (0 if offline or not yet received from Twitch).

followerCount.description: Real Twitch follower total (Get Channel Followers); 0 when the Helix read fails.

subscriberCount.description: Real Twitch subscriber total (Get Broadcaster Subscriptions); 0 when the Helix read fails.

chattersToday.description: Distinct chatters seen today (UTC) — the privacy-hashed ChannelChatterDays count.

supporterAmountMinorToday.description:

currency (string? DashboardStatsDto.SupporterCurrency); a mixed-currency day reports null rather than a

supporterCurrency.description: The single currency behind long? DashboardStatsDto.SupporterAmountMinorToday, else null.

platformsLive.description:

uptime.description: Stream uptime in whole seconds, null if offline.

Live fields come from the in-memory ChannelContext; counts are session totals since bot join.

sample.description: Up to a handful of the affected things' names, so the user recognises WHICH break.

A consequence a row count cannot express: something OUTSIDE our database stops working. Deleting a channel
revokes an overlay token every live OBS browser source is polling, drops EventSub subscriptions registered
with Twitch, and orphans channel-point rewards created under our client id — none of which is "N rows".
ConsequenceKey is an i18n resource KEY naming the effect ("N Twitch channel-point
rewards stop working"), never a table name and never a sentence.

FeatureFlagBlastRadius.description:
The counted blast radius of flipping a flag's GLOBAL toggle — shown to the operator BEFORE the toggle
commits (consequences-must-be-visible). int FeatureFlagBlastRadiusDto.TenantsAffected is the number of active channels
whose effective state is actually governed by the global toggle right now: an unexpired per-tenant
override insulates a channel from the global switch, so an overridden channel is never counted here — it
will not change. This is the same reasoning that makes a per-integration kill switch safe to flip: the
operator sees exactly how many tenants lose the integration, not an estimate.

FeatureStatus.description:

bool FeatureStatusDto.IsEnabled is the channel's OWN opt-in choice (row on, or the catalogue default), while
bool FeatureStatusDto.Entitled is whether the channel's tier / deployment / platform flag even ALLOWS the feature. A
feature is actually usable iff `Entitled && IsEnabled`; a not-entitled feature can still read
opt-in ON (legacy state), so the dashboard shows "Upgrade to unlock" (see string? FeatureStatusDto.RequiredTier) rather
than a toggle. An ungated feature is always bool FeatureStatusDto.Entitled.

LinkPolicy.description:
The rules of a `ChatFilterType.LinkPolicy` filter, stored as JSON in `ChatFilter.LinkPolicyJson`.

A link trips the filter unless its host is one of IReadOnlyList<string> LinkPolicy.AllowedDomains or a sub-domain of one.
With no allowed domain every link trips, which is how a filter behaved before it had a policy. Only links
written with a scheme (https://x.y) count, unless bool LinkPolicy.MatchBareDomains is on: then a bare
example.com counts too.

LocalizedText.description:
A typed reference to a backend-authored, user-facing translation KEY (S-SCHEMA-I18N-redesign). Backend schema
authors (widget settings fields, pipeline action field descriptors) construct one of these per label/help
string instead of a bare English literal or string parameter, so a schema-authoring call site cannot
accidentally pass raw English text where a translation key belongs. It carries no English or Dutch text —
translations live exclusively in the dashboard's existing i18n home
(`server/i18n/strings/values/strings.xml` for `en`, `values-nl/` for
`nl`), the single place a translator can find and edit every user-facing string in the product. The
dashboard resolves string LocalizedText.Key to display text via `core/i18n` (dots replaced with underscores to
match the Compose Resources string-name convention, e.g. `widget.alerts.events.label` →
`widget_alerts_events_label`). A committed key manifest (`server/i18n/schema-i18n-keys.manifest.json`)
plus paired backend/frontend guard tests fail the build if a key is authored here without both a `en` and
an `nl` entry in `strings.xml` — so a missing translation is caught at test time, never shipped as a
silent English fallback or, worse, an empty label. string? LocalizedText.Text is user-authored content shown as
written, never product text.

LockdownControl.description:
A room-tightening control (spam-defense.md §L5.1).

Every member restricts posting. There is deliberately no ban, timeout, or block member
in this enum: lockdown must not be able to express an action against a person, because SD0's whole
claim is that it costs everyone a few minutes and costs nobody their account.

renders only enabled providers, so there are never dead buttons. IReadOnlyList<string> LoginProviderDto.Flows are wire tokens
(`device_code` | `auth_code_pkce` | `auth_code`) telling the client which handshake to run.

ObsBatchExecution.description: OBS-WS RequestBatch execution types (wire values match obs-websocket v5).

ObsBridgeSetup.description: Everything the operator needs to install the browser-source bridge in OBS.

ObsBridgeStatus.description: One connected bridge's live status for a channel (obs-control.md §3.3).

ObsBrowserSource.description:
How a streamer sets up one overlay as an OBS browser source: the width and height to enter, whether to tick
"Control audio via OBS", and whether to tick "Shutdown source when not visible" (OBS then unloads the page, so
anything that must keep listening or playing leaves it off). Authored once per catalogue widget; a widget with no
catalogue entry (custom, community) carries none.

ObsConnection.description:
A channel's OBS connection as the dashboard sees it (obs-control.md §3). The OBS-WS password never
appears — only bool ObsConnectionDto.HasPassword — and the bridge token is surfaced solely through the
bridge-setup URL, never as a bare listing field.

ObsConnectionStatus.description:
The connection state a moderator panel needs to know whether OBS is switched on, and nothing of the
configuration: no host, port, password flags, event mask or error text (an error can carry the host).

ObsConnectionView.description: Which shape of the OBS connection a read returns (query option `view`).

ObsCurrentProfileRequest.description: REST body for the profile-select route: make one OBS profile the active one.

ObsCurrentSceneCollectionRequest.description: REST body for the scene-collection-select route: load one scene collection in OBS.

ObsCurrentTransitionRequest.description: REST body for the scene-transition-select route: make one transition the active one.

ObsFilter.description:
One filter attached to a source (obs-websocket v5 `GetSourceFilterList`) — name,
            kind, whether it's enabled, and its position in the source's filter chain. `filterSettings`
            is provider-specific free-form data the dashboard's filter list has no use for, so it's left out.

ObsFilterEnabledRequest.description: REST body for the filter-enable route: enable/disable one filter on one source.

ObsHotkeyTriggerRequest.description: REST body for the hotkey-trigger route.

ObsInputMuteRequest.description: REST body for the audio-mixer mute route: set an input's mute to an absolute state.

ObsInputVolumeRequest.description: REST body for the audio-mixer volume route: set an input's volume in decibels (OBS's dB scale).

ObsMediaActionRequest.description: REST body for the media-input-control route (play/pause/restart/stop/next/previous).

ObsProbe.description:
The truthful result of actively probing OBS reachability (obs-control.md §3.2). The passive
state/scenes/inputs reads mask a "not connected yet" as an empty 200 so the dashboard shows its connect
prompt instead of a scary 500 — which means a 200 there is NOT proof OBS is reachable. This probe instead
ATTEMPTS the transport and reports the real outcome: bool ObsProbeDto.Connected, plus the failing
string? ObsProbeDto.ErrorCode (`OBS_NOT_CONNECTED`, `OBS_DISABLED`, `OBS_BRIDGE_OFFLINE`,
`OBS_WRONG_MODE`) when it could not reach OBS. It is what lets the dashboard tell "connected" from the
masked empty state — for the direct socket and the bridge leader alike.

ObsProfile.description: One OBS profile (obs-websocket v5 `GetProfileList`), with the active one flagged.

ObsRecordRequest.description: REST body for the recording route.

ObsRefreshBrowserRequest.description: REST body for the browser-source-refresh route.

ObsRequest.description: One raw OBS-WS request (the generic pass-through surface).

ObsResponse.description: The outcome of one OBS-WS request as the caller sees it.

ObsSceneCollection.description: One scene collection (obs-websocket v5 `GetSceneCollectionList`), the loaded one flagged.

ObsSceneItem.description:
One item (source instance) placed in a scene — the per-scene visibility state
            ObsInputDto cannot express, since a global input can appear in several scenes with a
            different `sceneItemEnabled` in each.

ObsSceneItemEnabledRequest.description:
REST body for the scene-item visibility route: show/hide one item by its numeric id (two
            items in one scene can share a source name, so the id is the only exact handle).

ObsSceneItemLockedRequest.description: REST body for the scene-item lock route: lock/unlock one item in the OBS preview.

ObsSceneRequest.description: REST body for the scene-switch route.

ObsScreenshotRequest.description:
REST body for the source-screenshot route (obs-websocket v5 `GetSourceScreenshot`).
            ImageFormat is an encoder OBS supports (e.g. `png`, `jpg`).

ObsSourceVisibilityRequest.description: REST body for the per-source visibility route: hide/show one item within one scene.

ObsState.description: Live OBS state for the dashboard and the `{{obs.*}}` template vars.

ObsStats.description:
OBS performance stats (obs-websocket v5 `GetStats`) — CPU/memory load and the
            render-thread vs. output-thread frame counters, plus what OBS's own status bar adds from
            `GetStreamStatus` / `GetRecordStatus` / `GetVideoSettings`: the stream output's own
            skipped/total frames (OBS's "Dropped Frames"), byte counters (bitrate = delta between two reads),
            timecodes, congestion, and the target FPS.

ObsStudioModeRequest.description: REST body for the studio-mode route: turn studio mode on or off.

ObsStudioModeStatus.description:
Studio mode status (obs-websocket v5 `GetStudioModeEnabled`) — the same single-flag
            shape as ObsVirtualCamStatusDto.

ObsStudioTransitionRequest.description:
REST body for the studio-mode transition route: cut the preview scene to program.
            DurationMs is null to use the transition's own configured duration.

ObsToggle.description: Start/stop/toggle for OBS outputs (streaming, replay buffer, virtual cam).

ObsToggleRequest.description: REST body for start/stop/toggle output routes.

ObsTransition.description:
One scene transition OBS knows about (obs-websocket v5 `GetSceneTransitionList`) —
            mirrors ObsSceneDto's shape: name + whether it is the one currently selected.

ObsVendorRequest.description:
REST body for the vendor pass-through route (obs-websocket v5 `CallVendorRequest`) —
            the escape hatch for third-party OBS plugins that add their own vendor requests.

ObsVirtualCamStatus.description:
Virtual camera output status (obs-websocket v5 `GetVirtualCamStatus`) — the same
            single `outputActive` shape the stream/record/replay-buffer status requests answer with.

durationSeconds.description: Optional auto-close horizon in seconds (max 24h); null = open until closed manually.

announce.description: Announce the poll (question + numbered options + how to vote) in chat on open. Default true.

endpointId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

OutboundWebhookDelivery.description:
One row of an outbound endpoint's delivery log (webhooks.md §5.1) — the visibility that makes a webhook
integration debuggable: which event, which attempt, the resulting status/HTTP code, and the next retry time.
The rendered request body is intentionally omitted (it can carry sensitive payload); use the receiver's own logs.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

OutboundWebhookEventCatalogueEntry.description:
One subscribable business event in the outbound webhook catalogue (webhooks.md §9). The string OutboundWebhookEventCatalogueEntry.EventType
is the exact journaled event-type discriminator an endpoint puts in its `SubscribedEventTypes` (or `*`
for all); string OutboundWebhookEventCatalogueEntry.LabelKey and string OutboundWebhookEventCatalogueEntry.CategoryKey are dashboard string-resource keys (no prose —
the dashboard owns the translated text). Webhook-lifecycle events are deliberately absent — they are deny-listed to
prevent self-amplification.

requestedBy.description: The display name of the viewer who triggered the reply; null when nobody did.

highlight.description: A design token name (primary | success | warning | destructive); null = the widget accent.

durationSeconds.description: How long the line stays before it fades; null = the widget's own show time.

OverlayLine.description:
What a chat widget needs to draw a bot overlay line beyond its text: the viewer who asked for it (drawn as
"requested by ...", like the song request card; the line is never shown under the viewer's name) and the look
the channel chose. A null look value means the widget's default for that part.

channelId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

OverlayManifest.description:
The public, token-resolved overlay manifest (widgets-overlays.md §4). The single read an OBS browser source
needs: the channel's enabled, successfully-built widgets, each with the URL to fetch its compiled bundle, the
content hash (cache-bust key), its render-time trust tier, and its live settings + event subscriptions.

widgetId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

OverlayWidgetEntry.description:
One widget in the overlay manifest. string OverlayWidgetEntry.TrustTier (first_party | verified_community | unverified) is
derived from the widget's `Source` and drives the render-time CSP tier — a self-authored (custom) widget is
always `unverified` (fail-closed).
string? OverlayWidgetEntry.GalleryKey is the natural key of the gallery item the widget was made from (null for a widget with
none); it is how the host page recognises the system Audio widget without trusting a user setting.

PairingCode.description: A short-lived single-use pairing code the operator types (or scans) into the device.

PairingRedemption.description:
Everything a freshly-paired device needs to talk to this instance: where (string PairingRedemptionDto.BackendUrl),
as whom (string PairingRedemptionDto.Token — the one-time automation token secret, never retrievable again), and
what it may do (IReadOnlyList<string> PairingRedemptionDto.Scopes).

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

userId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

grantedByUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

PermitGrant.description:
A `!permit` grant for the permissions UI / audit (roles-permissions §4) — a per-user role grant or a
per-user capability grant (an action key), with its grantor, optional expiry, and revocation state.

PermitGrantType.description: Whether a `PermitGrant` grants a whole role or a single capability.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

PickList.description: The transport/read shape of a pick-list.

PickListPreview.description: A single sampled entry from a pick-list — backs the dashboard's "Test" button preview.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

parameterNames.description:
The named sub-pipeline parameters this pipeline declares (S-PIPE-TREE-d2b(a)), deserialized from
string? Pipeline.ParameterNamesJson — null/empty when the
pipeline declares none, in which case a caller's `run_pipeline` block falls back to positional
`args`. Surfaced so the pipeline builder can render one labelled field per declared name when this
pipeline is picked as a `run_pipeline` target, instead of a raw positional/generic argument list.

Pipeline.description: Full pipeline details including the deserialized node graph cache.

PipelineActionDescriptor.description: One available pipeline action block, for the builder's palette (commands-pipelines.md §3.13).

PipelineActionField.description:
One configuration field of a pipeline action block — drives which typed control the builder's step form
renders (S045) instead of a free-text box. `Kind` is the serialized name of a
PipelineActionFieldKind value (e.g. `"number"`,
`"enum"`, `"discord_channel"`). `Options` is populated only for `"enum"` fields.

PipelineBlastRadius.description:
The real, counted set of rows that reference a pipeline right now — surfaced in the delete
confirmation BEFORE the save, never estimated. int PipelineBlastRadiusDto.TotalReferences is zero exactly
when nothing references the pipeline; the dashboard must render that as an explicit
"nothing else references this" statement, not an empty/ambiguous state.

PipelineCatalogue.description:
The full palette the pipeline builder renders from — every registered action + condition, sourced from the
backend so the builder can never drift out of sync (replaces the hand-maintained frontend catalogue).

PipelineConditionDescriptor.description: One available pipeline condition type, for the builder's condition picker.

pipelineId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

triggeredByUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

PipelineExecutionDetail.description: Full run detail — the summary fields plus its ordered per-step logs.

PipelineExecutionHostCall.description: One host call a step made (for example `tts.speak`), with how long it took.

PipelineExecutionStepLog.description: One step's outcome within a run, so the FAILING step is identifiable in the detail read.

pipelineId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

triggeredByUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

PipelineExecutionSummary.description:
Lightweight run summary for the execution-history list view (H.4 PipelineExecution).
            `FailureKind` is null on a run that did not fail; `LimitKey` and `LimitValue` are set only
            when a limit or a time budget stopped the run.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

parameterNames.description:
See IReadOnlyList<string>? PipelineDto.ParameterNames — carried on the list item too so
            the `run_pipeline` target picker (fed by the list endpoint) knows a target's declared parameters without
            a second per-row fetch.

hasPlatformDefault.description:
True when the platform seeded this pipeline (e.g. the raid flows), so it can be restored to
            the platform default.

PipelineListItem.description: Lightweight pipeline summary for list views.

value.description: The stable id actually stored in the action's parameter (what gets persisted).

label.description: Human-readable name shown in the picker.

secondaryText.description:
What genuinely identifies this item in context beyond the label (cost, locale, duration, login vs display
name, …) — kind-specific, populated from the real source, never fabricated.

imageUrl.description: Optional preview/avatar/icon url; null when the source has none.

state.description: Whether the item is currently pickable.

reason.description: Populated when PipelineOptionState PipelineOption.State is PipelineOptionState.Unavailable.

PipelineOption.description:
One item a resource-picker field can offer, in the ONE generic shape every
PipelineActionFieldKind resource-picker kind returns — never a bespoke DTO per kind.

sourceAvailable.description: False when the underlying source is not connected/reachable for this tenant.

unavailableReason.description: Populated when bool PipelineOptionListResult.SourceAvailable is false.

items.description: The page of options; empty (with bool PipelineOptionListResult.SourceAvailable true) is a real empty list.

totalCount.description: Total items matching the search, for pagination — 0 when unavailable.

PipelineOptionListResult.description:
The result of resolving a picker kind's option list. bool PipelineOptionListResult.SourceAvailable distinguishes a
genuinely empty list (the tenant has zero rewards) from a source that could not be read at all (Discord not
linked, the guild call failed) — never collapsed into the same empty response (truthful-data rule).

PipelineOptionState.description: Whether one option can currently be picked (S-RICH-PICKERS).

PipelineTestRunRequest.description:
Seed variables for a pipeline dry-run (test-run) — no PII, author-supplied. Step is optional:
one action object (`{"type":"send_message", ...params}`); when set, only that action runs, through the
same capture engine, instead of the saved pipeline's graph. Graph is optional too: the draft
graph a person is editing (the same JSON the save takes); when set it is validated like a save and runs
instead of the saved graph, flat or tree. Nothing is stored.

PipelineTraceStep.description:
One row of a pipeline test-run trace: what one executed step did. `Branch` names the arm an `if` took
(`then`/`else`); `Iterations` is the pass count of a `loop`; `VariableChanges` lists only the
author's variables whose value changed; `Output` is what the step produced (e.g. the chat text it would send);
`Error` is set when the step failed. Rows are in the order the steps ran.

PipelineTraceVariableChange.description: One variable a traced step changed: the value before the step ran and the value after (null = unset).

PlatformAnalytics.description: SaaS-only cross-tenant platform stats (analytics.md §4) — no per-tenant identity crosses the boundary.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

uploadedByPrincipalId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

PlatformAudioAsset.description:
One platform audio file. string PlatformAudioAssetDto.PreviewUrl plays it in the browser; IReadOnlyList<string> PlatformAudioAssetDto.UsedByTemplates
names the non-retired templates that block its deletion (empty = deletable).

PlatformBotAdminStatus.description: The platform bot admin screen's read model — real state, read from the stored credential.

PlatformBotReconnectPollRequest.description: Body for polling a platform-bot reconnect — carries the same confirmation as the start call.

PlatformBotReconnectPreview.description:
The counted blast radius a platform-bot reconnect/replace would touch — every channel that has no
active custom bot of its own and therefore speaks through the shared platform bot. Must be rendered
before a reconnect is armed, and re-verified fresh (not trusted from a stale preview) when the swap
actually applies.

PlatformBotReconnectRequest.description: Body for starting a platform-bot reconnect — the confirmed count MUST match a fresh preview.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

latestDraftVersionId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

PlatformContentDefinition.description: A platform content definition summary row (platform-admin.md §3.1) — the definitions list.

PlatformContentDefinitionDetail.description: A definition plus its full version history (§4 `GET /definitions/{id}`).

PlatformContentInstallSummary.description:
What the definition's installed copies look like across every tenant right now: how many exist, how many
were copied from an older version than the current one, and how many the channel has edited since (an
update-in-place publish never overwrites those). Counted from the real rows, the same way the publish
preview counts them.
