PlatformDefaultBlastRadius.description:
The counted consequence of changing one platform default, shown BEFORE the save (consequences must be
visible). ChannelsAffected is the active channels that follow the platform default and
would therefore feel the change (0 when the proposed value equals the current one);
ChannelsKeepingOwnSetting is the active channels whose own setting keeps winning.
RequiresDangerConfirmation is true when the default guards a dangerous action, so the
save must carry an explicit confirmation. The save echoes ChannelsAffected back and is
refused as stale when the live count has moved since.

PlatformDefaultChange.description:
One part of a row that a restore replaces. string PlatformDefaultChangeDto.Field is a stable key the dashboard labels
(timer: `name`, `messages`, `interval`, `min_chat_activity`, `enabled`,
`fire_once`; pipeline: `steps`, `step_settings`); the values are shown as-is.

rowId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

PlatformDefaultPreview.description:
The consequence of restoring one row to its platform default. int? PlatformDefaultPreviewDto.InstalledVersion is the
version the row was installed or last synced from; int PlatformDefaultPreviewDto.DefaultVersion is what a restore writes.
bool PlatformDefaultPreviewDto.IsEdited is true when the channel changed the row since then. IReadOnlyList<PlatformDefaultChangeDto> PlatformDefaultPreviewDto.Changes lists
each part that differs from the default — empty means a restore changes nothing.

definitionId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

PlatformTemplate.description: One published platform template a channel can install (its current published version).

rowId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

definitionId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

PlatformTemplateUpdate.description:
One installed copy and the version its definition is on now. bool PlatformTemplateUpdateDto.EditedSinceInstall is true when
the channel changed the copy after it was installed: taking the update replaces those edits.

PlatformViewer.description:
A Twitch account resolved straight from the platform by login (Helix Get Users) — for a person the bot
has never seen, so a streamer can ban or time them out ahead of time. `Id` is the Twitch user id
the moderation writes consume.

PlayerButton.description:
One button the streamer pinned to the Now playing panel. Pressing it runs ActionType with
Parameters through the channel action runner. Icon is a dashboard icon
key (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens). Id is assigned by the server when empty.

gameConfigId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

playerUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

PlayGameRequest.description: Play a game (economy.md §4). int PlayGameRequest.RoleLevel is the caller's resolved community level.

PollPredictionHistoryItem.description:
One poll or prediction the channel ran, with its final result, folded from the event journal.
Kind is `poll` or `prediction`. Status is the Twitch end status
(completed, archived, terminated, resolved, canceled) or `unfinished` when the journal holds a start but no end.

id.description: The Twitch choice or outcome id.

votes.description: Poll: total votes (normal plus channel points). Prediction: number of users who picked it.

channelPoints.description: Poll: votes cast with channel points. Prediction: points put on it.

sharePercent.description: This option's share of all votes, 0 to 100, rounded to a whole number.

isWinner.description: True for the winning choice or outcome.

PollPredictionOption.description: One choice (poll) or outcome (prediction) of a past poll or prediction.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

PricedUnit.description:
The owner-authored price of one usage unit. long PricedUnitDto.PriceMinorUnitsPerBatch is charged per
long PricedUnitDto.BatchSize raw units of string PricedUnitDto.UnitKey — a real cost of a fraction of a minor unit
per raw unit (e.g. TTS characters, sandbox milliseconds) is represented exactly by pricing a batch of
them, never by a float.

Project.description:
The multi-file project the editor loads and saves (dev-platform.md §4.2, §8): a widget or script is a
Dictionary<string, string> ProjectDto.Files set (`path → content`) plus its ProjectManifestDto ProjectDto.Manifest. This is the wire shape the
`GET/PUT .../project` endpoints round-trip — identical whether the artifact is one file or a full
`src/` tree. On `PUT` the server re-builds from these before persisting a version (never trusting a
client bundle), so the file set + manifest ARE the source of truth.

ProjectionRebuildResult.description: How many events one named projection applied during a rebuild.

ProjectManifest.description:
The project manifest on the wire (dev-platform.md §4.2) — `{ entry, kind, framework, dependencies[] }`.
A one-to-one DTO for ProjectManifest; kept distinct from the domain record so the Application
contract and the stored manifest can evolve independently.

PronounCatalog.description: Catalog entry as returned by the public catalog endpoint.

platform.description: The platform the check is about, or null when it covers the whole channel.

reason.description: Plain English: why the check is in this state, and what is missing when it is not ok.

ProtectionCheck.description: One protection check and its current state.

checks.description: Every check, in a stable order.

ProtectionStatus.description:
Whether protection is running for one channel: one check per thing a streamer relies on. A check that
could not be read is reported as string ProtectionCheckStates.Unknown, never as healthy.

appDecisionRecorded.description:
True when the operator made a DELIBERATE recorded choice for this provider — their own app, or an
explicit decision to use the shared one. A shipped config default alone is never enough.

supported.description: False for providers whose credentials this build has no way to use.

apiKeySource.description:
Which source supplies the YouTube Data API key (stored, environment or unset); null for every other
provider, which has no API key. The key itself is never carried.

botTokenSource.description:
Which source supplies the Discord bot's own token (stored, environment or unset); null for every other
provider, which has no bot token. The token itself is never carried.

ProviderCredential.description:
One provider's app-credential state for the operator console.

The secret is never in here, in any form. It is sealed under an AAD tied to its provider and
field, and there is no read path that unseals it for display — only string ProviderCredentialDto.SecretSource, which says
whether one exists and which source would win. The client id IS carried: it is a public identifier that
appears in every OAuth URL the viewer's own browser sees, and hiding it would only stop the operator
checking the one value most likely to be wrong.

PublicChannel.description:
One channel in the deployment's public directory (chat-client.md §9a "Reaching any channel"): only what
the channel shows every visitor on Twitch. No role, no settings, no tokens. `OnBot` is false for a
Twitch channel this deployment does not serve; its `Id` is then the Twitch user id, not a tenant Guid.

PublicInvite.description:
What an invite link gives, for a signed-out visitor (S-INVITE-TIER). An unknown, used-up, expired or revoked
code all read the same (not usable, one fixed reason, no tier), so a guesser cannot tell which codes exist.
Reading never spends a redemption.

internalUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

PublishPreview.description: The blast-radius preview (§2.1) — must be rendered before a confirm button enables.

PublishSubmission.description: A publish submission in the vetting queue: `pending` | `approved` | `rejected` (+ reason).

itemId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

buyerUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

QueueItem.description:
A queue item with its zero-based position and the number viewers see
            (QueueNumbering — the one `!queue` prints and `!wrongsong N` reads back).
            Cost is 0 for a free request.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

userId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

Quote.description: The transport/read shape of a quote (quotes.md §3).

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

RaidBalanceWeights.description:
Points when they raided us more than we raided them: the base for one owed raid, the extra for
each further one, and the points when raids are level.

RaidCategoryRule.description: A liked category: its name, its points and the reason text.

RaidKeywordRule.description:
A signal made of plain words or phrases. A word matches a whole tag, or whole words in the
title, ignoring case and punctuation. No regular expression is involved.

RaidRecencyRules.description: Points by time since the last outgoing raid: never, within each step, or older than all steps.

RaidRecencyStep.description: A raid that happened less than WithinDays days ago.

preferredCategories.description: Categories this channel likes, matched by name ignoring case, first match wins.

otherCategoryWeight.description: Points for a category that is not in PreferredCategories.

otherCategoryLabel.description: Reason text for that case; the category name is appended in brackets.

keywords.description: Tag and title signals, checked in order, first matching rule wins.

viewerBands.description: Viewer-count bands, checked in order, first band that holds the count wins.

recency.description: How long ago this channel last raided the candidate.

followedWeight.description: Points when the broadcaster follows the candidate.

RaidScoringRules.description:
One channel's raid-target preferences. The scorer owns no rule of its own: every point it hands
out comes from this object. A rule with weight 0 adds nothing and shows no reason. A key a stored
blob or request body leaves out takes its value from RaidScoringDefaults; pass the
deserialized object through RaidScoringRules RaidScoringDefaults.Resolve(RaidScoringRules? raw) before use.

RaidViewerBand.description: A viewer-count band, both ends included.

RedeemInviteCodeResult.description:
The result of redeeming an invite code. DateTime? RedeemInviteCodeResultDto.GrantedTierExpiresAt is when the gifted tier ends;
null with a tier is a forever gift.

RedeemPairingCodeRequest.description: Body of `POST /automation/v1/pair` — the code IS the credential.

RedemptionListItem.description:
One entry in the channel-points redemption queue (rewards.md) — a redemption with its current
            status (`unfulfilled` / `fulfilled` / `canceled`), folded from the journal.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

RedemptionTimer.description:
One live/recent countdown for a time-limited reward redemption. `RemainingSeconds` is
            the CURRENT clock-derived value; `Status` is running | paused | completed | canceled.

RefreshTokenRequest.description:
Token refresh request. The refresh token is optional in the body: the served-web dashboard sends none and
relies on the HttpOnly cookie the browser attaches automatically, while native clients send the token they
hold in their own vault. A native client acting as another user also sends the act-as token it holds
(string? RefreshTokenRequest.ActAsToken, possibly expired): while that session is open the refresh hands back the SAME
impersonated user, never the operator. The served-web dashboard keeps that token in an HttpOnly cookie.

actorUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

ReinstateTenantRequest.description: Body for the reinstate action — the justification lands in the audit row.

RemovedSongs.description: How many queued songs a bulk removal took out.

RemoveRequesterSongs.description: Request to remove every queued song of one requester (display name, case-insensitive).

RenderManifest.description:
Everything the dashboard shell needs to render for the active channel, aggregated into one
            response so the client boots with a single request instead of four. Each section reuses the same
            DTO its dedicated endpoint returns:
            * ResolvedAccessDto RenderManifestDto.Access — the caller's resolved access (roles/effective/me).
* IReadOnlyList<FeatureStatusDto> RenderManifestDto.Features — the channel's feature toggles (features).
* IReadOnlyList<ChannelIntegrationDto> RenderManifestDto.Integrations — integration connection states (integrations).
* MissingScopesDto RenderManifestDto.Scopes — outstanding Twitch scope gaps (twitch/diagnostics/missing-scopes).ResolvedAccessDto RenderManifestDto.Access is always resolved (self-introspection) and is load-bearing. The feature,
            integration, and scope sections are each populated ONLY when the caller clears that surface's
            Gate-2 read floor (per their IReadOnlyList<string> ResolvedAccessDto.HeldActionKeys) — a participant sees
            them empty — so the aggregate never leaks data an individual endpoint would have withheld. Of the
            entitled sections, features is load-bearing (a real failure fails the manifest); integrations and
            scopes degrade to an empty section instead.

ReorderMediaRequest.description: Reorder body — the new 1-based play position (media-share.md §5).

ReplayActivityResult.description:
What a replay actually re-performed — every count is real work, and 0 is a valid, truthful
    outcome (e.g. the response is disabled, or every subscribed widget was removed since the alert fired),
    never disguised as a full success. EventsReplayed is 1, or 1 + each named recipient of a gift bomb.

ReplyDelivery.description:
How a channel-authored reply is delivered. bool ReplyDelivery.Html makes the overlay line render the authored
text as sanitized HTML; the platform chat always gets plain text. A missing value everywhere means
ReplyDelivery ReplyDelivery.ChatOnly, the behavior before this setting existed.

ReplyLook.description:
How a reply looks on the chat overlay: an optional highlight color (a design token name), a size, and how long
the line stays before it fades. A missing value means the overlay's own default for that part, so a null look
changes nothing about the line.

ReplySize.description: How big a chat overlay line is drawn.

ReplyTarget.description: Where an authored reply goes: the platform chat, the chat overlay, both, or nowhere.

subjectUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

broadcasterId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

RequiredOverlay.description:
One channel-owned system surface (widgets-overlays.md §1.2) for the OBS page's Required overlays panel.
string RequiredOverlay.Key is the surface's stable catalogue key (`audio`, `alerts`, ...) so the client can
name and describe it in the viewer's language; WidgetDetail RequiredOverlay.Widget is the provisioned widget.

userId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

broadcasterId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

ResolvedAccess.description:
The full breakdown of a caller's resolved authorization for a channel (roles-permissions §4) — each
plane's contributing level and the winning source — for the permissions UI and debugging.
`EffectiveLevel` is `MAX(CommunityLevel, ManagementLevel, permit-role level)`.
PermitCapabilities are the caller's per-USER capability grants only. HeldActionKeys is the
broader, UI-facing set: EVERY action key in the catalogue the caller actually CLEARS on this channel —
their EffectiveLevel meets the action's channel-effective required level (which FOLDS IN the
broadcaster's ChannelActionOverride, unlike the per-plane level fields), OR they hold a direct
per-user capability grant for it. The dashboard gates page/action visibility on this set.

followUp.description: Follow-up against the sender after a deny: `none` (default), `timeout` or `ban`.

timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout length in seconds (1–1209600), required when string? ResolveModerationQueueItemRequest.FollowUp is `timeout`.

reason.description: Optional reason recorded with a `timeout`/`ban` follow-up.

ResolveModerationQueueItemRequest.description:
A moderator resolves a held AutoMod message — `approve` (release it to chat) or `deny` (drop it).
A deny may carry a follow-up moderation action against the sender: `timeout` (requires
int? ResolveModerationQueueItemRequest.TimeoutSeconds) or `ban`, each with an optional string? ResolveModerationQueueItemRequest.Reason.

ResolveUnbanRequestRequest.description:
Approve or deny a pending unban request, with an optional note the viewer sees. Approving reverses a
ban instantly and irreversibly (from the dashboard's perspective — Twitch offers no "re-ban on regret"), so
bool ResolveUnbanRequestRequest.Confirm must be explicitly set true on approval; a bare `Approve: true` with no confirmation
is rejected rather than acted on. Denial carries no such risk and needs no confirmation.

ResolveViewerReportRequest.description: A moderator resolves a report — `dismiss` (no action) or `escalate` (they then act via the ban/timeout tools).

ResourceClass.description:
Classifies a limited resource by whether it maps to a real marginal cost (S-BUDGETS-a). The owner's binding
intent: limits exist to recover real cost, never to manufacture upsell pressure.

ResourceUsage.description:
One `LimitedResourceRegistry` entry's truthful current state (S-BUDGETS-b1) — the read-side mirror of
what `IResourceQuotaService.CheckAsync` would evaluate for the NEXT write. long ResourceUsageDto.CurrentCount
comes from the exact same counting source enforcement uses, never a second query, so this can never disagree
with what a save would allow. ResourceClass ResourceUsageDto.Class is carried explicitly so a UI can never mistake a NEAR_FREE
abuse floor for a paid ceiling. long ResourceUsageDto.Limit is `-1` when unlimited (every self-host
COST_DRIVING resource); NEAR_FREE resources are NEVER tier-scaled, so long ResourceUsageDto.Limit always equals
long ResourceUsageDto.SafetyBaseline for them, on every tenant including self-host — long ResourceUsageDto.SafetyBaseline is
unused (0) for COST_DRIVING.

RewardAvailability.description: Whether the channel can have channel points: Twitch gives them to Affiliates and Partners only.

pipelineId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

internalUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

SaveProviderCredentialRequest.description:
A credential write. Both fields optional and independent: sending only a secret rotates the secret and
leaves the id alone, which is the common case. A BLANK field means "leave it", never "clear it" — clearing
is `DELETE`, so a half-filled form can never silently wipe a working credential.
ApiKey is the YouTube Data API key and is accepted for the youtube provider only.
BotToken is the Discord bot's own token (Developer Portal, Bot tab) and is accepted for the
discord provider only.

SaveSharedBanSettingsRequest.description: Both switches are explicit on every save — no partial policy writes (opt-in, default-deny).

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

ownerBroadcasterId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

ScopeRegrantStart.description:
A started re-grant device authorization (identity-auth §3.4a): the same secret-free Device Code Flow the
streamer login uses, but requesting `granted ∪ missing` so the existing grant is never dropped. The
client shows string ScopeRegrantStartDto.UserCode at string ScopeRegrantStartDto.VerificationUri and polls the normal streamer device
poll with string ScopeRegrantStartDto.DeviceCode; on approval the token store reconciles the new scopes and the gap clears.

ScriptSourcePosition.description:
A place in the author's own source: the project file, and the line and column in it. Both numbers start at 1,
the way an editor shows them. string? ScriptSourcePosition.File is null when the file is not known.

ScriptTestRunRequest.description:
The inputs to a script dry-run (test-run): the seed variables and positional args the author supplies to
exercise the script's current version without causing real side effects. string? ScriptTestRunRequest.Trigger (a
string TriggerSample.Id) seeds the triggering user and the variables a live event sets; the request's own
IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> ScriptTestRunRequest.Variables win over the sample's. string? ScriptTestRunRequest.Role is the viewer role written to `user.role`.

code.description: A stable code for the kind of rejection, for programs to match on.

message.description: The reason in plain words, for the author to read.

line.description: The line in the script where the problem is. Null when it has no single line.

column.description: The column in that line where the problem starts. Null when it has no single column.

file.description: The project file the line and column belong to. Null when unknown (older stored errors).

SeCommand.description:
A StreamElements custom command. `AccessLevel` is SE's numeric permission ladder
(0=everyone … 100=subscriber … 500=broadcaster), mapped to this project's role ladder on import.
SE separates a global `Cooldown` from a per-user `UserCooldown` (both in seconds).

SeQuote.description: A StreamElements quote. `AddedBy` is the attributed author; `Game` the context category.

SetActionDefaultRequest.description:
Sets (or, with a null Level, clears) the platform default for one action.
ConfirmedChannelsAffected must equal the preview's live count, and
ConfirmDanger must be true for a Critical/ToS-tier action.

SetAnalyticsOptOutRequest.description: Body for the viewer analytics opt-out toggle (analytics.md §5).

SetBuiltinReplyDefaultRequest.description: Saves a reply text. ConfirmedChannelsAffected must equal the preview's live count.

SetChannelNamePronunciation.description: Request to set how TTS says the channel's name. Empty or blank clears it.

SetChannelPersonalityRequest.description: Request to set a channel's built-in-command personality tone.

SetChannelSpotifyCredentials.description: Request body to store a channel's own Spotify app credentials.

SetEventResponseDefaultRequest.description: Saves a platform default. ConfirmedChannelsAffected must equal the preview's live count.

SetFeatureFlagOverrideRequest.description: Set a per-tenant override (the internal/beta opt-in or per-channel kill-switch).

SetFeatureFlagRequest.description: Create-or-update a flag's global definition (rollout-updates §5 ramp controls).

SetHttpEgressAllowlistEnabledRequest.description: Switch an approved host on or off.

SetModerationStandingRequest.description: Request body for setting a viewer's bot-side standing.

pronounId.description: The int Pronoun.Id to set as primary, or `null` to leave unchanged, or `0` to clear.

altPronounId.description: The int Pronoun.Id to set as alt, or `null` to leave unchanged, or `0` to clear.

manualOverride.description: When `true`, pin this choice and prevent automatic provider resolution from overwriting it.

SetPronounRequest.description: Request to set or clear pronouns for the authenticated viewer.

userId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

SetSuspiciousStatusRequest.description: Flag a chatter as suspicious — `active_monitoring` (watch) or `restricted` (their messages are held).

SetTenantLimitOverrideRequest.description: Body for setting a per-tenant quota exception (S-ADMIN-3). `LimitValue = -1` means unlimited.

region.description: Azure only — the Cognitive Services region the key belongs to.

SetTtsByokKey.description: Request to store a BYOK provider API key; the key is vault-encrypted at rest and never echoed.

SetTtsVoiceDefaultRequest.description: Saves the platform default voice. ConfirmedChannelsAffected must equal the preview's live count.

SetupAction.description:
How a UI completes a step. `Type` is `save_credentials` (POST/PUT the IReadOnlyList<SetupFieldDto> SetupStepDto.Fields
to `Endpoint`) or `oauth_redirect` (GET `Endpoint` for a URL to send the browser to, then poll
`PollEndpoint` for completion).

SetupField.description: One input the user fills in for a step (key, label, control type, required flag, help text).

SetupStep.description: One onboarding step: presentation + live state + the action and fields that complete it.

SetupWizard.description:
The self-describing first-time-setup contract a dashboard renders the onboarding flow from: an ordered list of
steps plus an overall bool SetupWizardDto.Complete flag. Each step carries everything the UI needs — copy, the exact
redirect URI to register, the API call that satisfies it, the input fields, and its live completion state — so
the onboarding pages need no hardcoded knowledge of the steps.

SetUserVoice.description: Request to assign a specific TTS voice to a viewer.

SharedBanSettings.description: The channel's shared-ban policy + its trust list (moderation.md §3.5 / §4).

trustedChannelId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

addedByUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

SharedBanTrustedChannel.description: One trusted partner row (J.9a) with its display name for the trust-list UI.

ShieldMode.description: Whether the channel's Twitch Shield Mode is active.

displayName.description: The name as Twitch shows it.

color.description: The chat color from their latest chat line in this channel, or null when none is known.

lastCategory.description: The category of their channel on Twitch now (Get Channel Information), or null when none is set.

streamsLast30Days.description: How many archived streams they published in the last 30 days (Get Videos, type archive).

lastShoutoutAt.description: When this channel last shouted them out, from our own records, or null when never.

profileImageUrl.description: The chatter's Twitch profile picture (Get Users), or null when Twitch gave none.

ShoutoutSuggestion.description: One chatter of the current stream the streamer may want to shout out.

SongHistoryItem.description:
One accepted song request in the channel's history. TrackName is empty for a row that
was rebuilt from the journal, which carries only the uri.

SongRequest.description: Request to add a song to the queue.

broadcasterId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

SongRequestPage.description:
The channel context a public SR-page token resolves to (music-sr.md §3.7) — everything the anonymous
`/sr/{token}` page needs to render and gate the submit form, with no JWT and no PII.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.
Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

SpamCampaign.description:
One correlated cohort, for the Campaigns surface.

DateTime? SpamCampaignDto.ReversedAt null and int SpamCampaignDto.RestoredAccountCount zero means no reversal was
ever attempted; DateTime? SpamCampaignDto.ReversedAt null with int SpamCampaignDto.RestoredAccountCount positive or
string SpamCampaignDto.RestorationFailedAccountIds non-empty means an attempt fell short of every actioned
account; DateTime? SpamCampaignDto.ReversedAt set means every actioned account came back. Three distinct,
legible states — a partial restore must never be indistinguishable from either extreme.

SpamConfidence.description: How sure the stack is, per SD1.

SpamDefensePolicy.description:
The whole configuration surface in one response: the channel's current values, the metadata to
render an editor for them, and the guarantees that have no switch.

They travel together on purpose. A client that fetched values alone would have to hardcode
its own idea of the bounds, and the first time a range moved server-side the form would start
rejecting saves it had just accepted.

isEnabled.description: Kill switch for the whole stack.

dryRun.description:
Detect and log, act on nothing. On for a channel's first 7 days, and a perfectly good permanent
setting for a channel that only wants visibility.

trustThresholds.description: Thresholds for the earned ladder and the SD8 immunity gate.

semiTrustedWatchHoursHere.description: Watch hours in this channel that grant Semi-Trusted.

semiTrustedWatchHoursInstance.description: Watch hours across this instance's channels that grant Semi-Trusted.

accountAgeGateDays.description: Hold chat from accounts younger than this many days. 0 is off.

followAgeGateDays.description: Hold chat from followers who followed less than this many days ago. 0 is off.

accountGateHoldsForReview.description: A gated message waits for a moderator (true) or is removed outright (false).

nearDuplicateSimilarity.description: Similarity at which a message counts as a mutation of a known campaign.

minimumSkeletonLength.description: Skeletons shorter than this are never corpus-matched.

nonLatinScriptGate.description: Restrict non-Latin script to viewers who have been around. Off by default (SD2).

qualifyNoStandingShare.description: Share of a cohort with no standing needed to call it a campaign.

dequalifyNoStandingShare.description: Share below which a qualified cohort is exonerated and reversed.

minimumCohortSize.description: Fewest distinct accounts that can constitute a campaign.

windowSeconds.description: Correlation window, extended by each new match.

maxWindowSeconds.description: Hard cap on the correlation window, from the first match.

actionDelaySeconds.description: The exoneration head start before a qualified campaign may act.

autoReverseOnDequalify.description: Undo a campaign's actions when it de-qualifies. Off is allowed, and warned against.

followSpikeFactor.description: Follow rate over the channel's own baseline that counts as a spike.

joinBurstFactor.description: Chatter-join rate over the channel's own baseline that counts as a burst.

lockdownMinutes.description: How long a lockdown holds before restoring the room by itself.

lockdownAutoExtend.description: Extend the window while the attack is still arriving.

lockdownMaxMinutes.description: Ceiling on a lockdown however long the attack lasts.

networkSubscribe.description: Pull the shared signature set. Free, read-only, and on by default.

networkContribute.description: Send this channel's confirmed signatures back. Opt-in (SD3).

requiredCorroborations.description: Independent reporters needed before a quarantined signature may act.

SpamDefenseSettings.description:
Every knob in the spam-defence stack (spam-defense.md §6.1).

Nothing in this design is a magic number buried in code. Every threshold named anywhere in the
spec is a stored, editable setting with a documented default, a range, and a plain-language
explanation of what moving it costs — see SpamSettingCatalogue, which is enforced
against this record by test so a knob cannot ship without its explanation.The same record is edited at two scopes: per channel, and as the platform-wide defaults every
new channel inherits. Same fields, same validation, same copy — only the scope differs.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

SpamDetection.description: One recorded verdict, for the review queue.

SpamInvariant.description: A protection the operator gets for free and cannot turn off.

SpamOutcome.description: What the engine decided to do. Ordered so a stricter outcome is a larger value.

SpamSettingDescriptor.description:
One knob as the editor needs it: what it is, where it belongs, and what it is bounded to.
The words come from the dashboard's string resources, keyed by these. A setting the engine does
not read yet carries the slice that wires it and the key for why it has no effect.

SpamTrustTier.description: The spam-defence trust ladder (spam-defense.md §L4). Ladder-valued so comparisons are ordinary numeric ones, matching the existing permission ladder. Users never see these numbers — the dashboard shows tier NAMES, per the role-name rule.

StartLiveGameRequest.description: Start a round of `GameType` for the channel.

StreamAnalytics.description:
One stream's per-stream aggregates — the "stream by stream, not all-time" analytics view. Counts are
window-folded from the raw activity between DateTimeOffset? StreamAnalyticsDto.StartedAt and DateTimeOffset? StreamAnalyticsDto.EndedAt (or now,
while the stream is still live); int? StreamAnalyticsDto.PeakViewers is the fold the status poller stamps.

StreamElementsExport.description:
A tolerant view of a StreamElements chatbot export (the JSON a streamer downloads from their SE bot
dashboard). Every field is nullable and every collection optional so a partial or older export never fails
to bind — missing sections simply import nothing. Only the commands / quotes / timers surfaces are read;
overlays and widgets are out of scope (a future import).

StreamListItem.description: One stream in the channel's history list, newest first — the per-stream entry point.

streamId.description: The stream the recap belongs to.

fromAt.description: Start of the window the recap counts.

toAt.description: End of the window the recap counts.

updatedAt.description: When the recap was last built.

outputWidth.description: Width in pixels of the stream output the recap was made at; null when none was stored (the dashboard labels its fallback).

outputHeight.description: Height in pixels of the stream output the recap was made at; null when none was stored.

stats.description: The recap data, exactly as the widget got it.

StreamRecap.description: One stream's kept recap: the window it counts and the same data the raid recap widget receives.

stream.description: The stream these numbers belong to.

oneOf.description: Who streamed: the channel's display name and profile picture, for headers and watermarks.

duration.description: Seconds from the start of the stream to its end (or to now while live).

peakViewers.description: The highest viewer count the stream recorded.

newFollowers.description: Display names of the viewers who followed during the stream, oldest first.

oneOf.description: Subscriptions during the stream: new, resubscribed, gifted and the total.

gifters.description: Gifters by gift count; anonymous gifts are merged as "Anonymous".

selfSubs.description: Viewers who subscribed or resubscribed themselves (gift recipients excluded), in order.

oneOf.description: Total bits and the top cheerers (count = bits).

raidsIn.description: Raids that arrived during the stream: who raided and with how many viewers.

oneOf.description: The hype trains that ended during the stream. Absent when there was none.
Redemption total and the top reward titles.
Song request total and the top requesters; never song titles.
Chat message count and the number of different chatters.

topChatters.description: The chatters with the most messages.

oneOf.description: Commands run in the window and the most-used ones.

StreamStats.description:
The answer to `stream-stats`: the stream window plus one named property per requested metric key. A metric
that was not requested (or has nothing to show, such as the peak of a stream that never recorded one) is omitted.
A new metric adds a property here and a class implementing `IStreamMetric`; never an endpoint.

avatarUrl.description: The channel profile picture URL. Null when the platform gave none.

StreamStatsChannel.description: The channel a stream belongs to.

level.description: The highest level any hype train reached.

trains.description: How many hype trains ended during the stream.

StreamStatsHypeTrain.description: The hype trains that ended during a stream.

viewers.description: How many viewers came with the raid.

StreamStatsRanked.description: A total and its top entries, ranked by count then name.

id.description: The stream id.

endedAt.description: When the stream ended. Null while it is live.

StreamStatsWindow.description: The window of one stream: its id, start, end, title and game.

SubmitGalleryItemRequest.description: A community widget submission (widgets-overlays.md §3.3): GitHub-pinned source, never pulled at HEAD.

resolves, plus the LIVE operator comps (`EntitlementGrant`) behind it. IReadOnlyList<SupportPersonEntitlementGrantDto> SupportPersonEntitlementDto.Grants is empty

One person matched by the cross-tenant support search (S-ADMIN-7a). Identity only — the per-tenant facts
live on SupportPersonViewDto, behind a second audited lookup.

SupportPersonView.description:
ONE cross-tenant view of one person's REAL state (S-ADMIN-7a). Every list is sourced from its own table
and every per-tenant fact names the tenant it belongs to. A datum the system does not have for this person
is ABSENT — an empty list, never a zeroed placeholder row that would read as real data.

SuspiciousStatus.description: A chatter's suspicious-user status after an add/clear, read back from Twitch — the resulting status and any monitoring types.

SystemStatus.description:
bool SystemStatusDto.OnboardingComplete is the ONLY gate the client routes onboarding vs. login off. It means
the operator has made a DELIBERATE, RECORDED decision about at least one platform's app — either BYOC
(their own client id, saved) or an explicit "use the shared app" choice — never an incidental config/env
fallback (the shipped public Twitch client id) alone. It is deployment-level setup, not who is signed in
and not whether the platform bot is authorized. Bot authorization is per-channel work that happens after
login; its live state is CheckItem SystemChecks.PlatformBot, reported separately so the wizard can
still show it without it ever blocking the client from reaching the login screen.

TemplateHelper.description:
Wire shape for one entry of `GET /api/v1/templates/helpers?context=` (S042). string TemplateHelperDto.Key is
the placeholder text as written in a template; string TemplateHelperDto.DescriptionKey is the i18n key the
dashboard resolves for display — never resolved English text (the backend never ships English
literals for user-facing strings).

targetBroadcasterId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

TenantAccessGrant.description: An audited support-access grant — a time-boxed, tenant-narrowed role assignment (stream-admin.md §4).

userId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

TenantMember.description:
One person who belongs to a tenant, for the operator's act-as picker: the owner, a management member, a
community member or a viewer the channel has seen. Relation is `owner`,
`manager`, `community` or `viewer`; the role and standing are NAMES, never numbered levels.

TenantRemigrationResult.description:
Outcome of an operator-forced re-application of pending EF Core migrations (S-ADMIN-3) — a database-wide
recovery lever, not a per-tenant DDL operation (the schema is shared). Reports what was pending
immediately before the call and what is still pending immediately after, so a caller can tell a genuine
"already up to date" from a real apply.

TestChatFilterRequest.description: Dry-runs a pattern the dashboard editor is not (yet) saving, against one sample message.

timeline.description: Every effect, chat message and console line in the order it happened; empty when the run kind has none.

trace.description: What each executed step did, in run order (pipeline test-runs only; empty for scripts).

oneOf.description: Where in the author's own file a failed script run threw; null when the run passed or the place is unknown.

TestRunResult.description:
The uniform result of a script or pipeline test-run (custom-code.md / commands-pipelines.md). The logic ran for
real; every outward/mutating effect was CAPTURED (see IReadOnlyList<CapturedEffectDto> TestRunResultDto.CapturedEffects) rather than committed, while
read-only calls (reads, conditions, template resolution, random draws) ran against the live services so the
dry-run stays realistic.

TestTrigger.description: One trigger sample the editor offers for a test run (`GET code-scripts/test-triggers`).

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

Tier.description: A public billing plan with its limits.

TierChangePreview.description:
The counted blast radius of editing a tier that already has tenants on it (platform-admin.md's
counted-preview shape, mirrored from platform content publish). int TierChangePreviewDto.AffectedTenantCount is the
real, live count of tenants with an active/trialing subscription on the tier RIGHT NOW — never estimated.
A save must echo this count back as `ConfirmedAffectedTenantCount`; a save whose confirmed count no
longer matches a freshly recomputed one fails closed (`PREVIEW_STALE`), the same rule platform-content
publish already enforces.

TierLimit.description: One quota lever for a tier (`-1` = unlimited).

TimelineEntry.description:
One row of a test-run timeline: everything the run would have done outwardly, in the order it happened.
`Seq` counts from 1; `Kind` is `chat`, `effect` or `console`; `Text` is the chat
message, the console line, or `name: argsPreview` for an effect.

pipelineId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

oneOf.description: Where a message timer's line goes and whether the overlay line is HTML; null = the platform chat as plain text.
What a firing runs when bound directly: a command, an action or a pipeline. Null for a plain message timer.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

hasPlatformDefault.description: True when the timer was installed from a platform template, so it can be restored to it.

TimerListItem.description: Lightweight timer info for list views.

TopCommand.description:
One command in the "what chat runs" ranking: long TopCommandDto.Uses counts the runs that worked,
int TopCommandDto.Users the distinct people who ran it, long TopCommandDto.Failed the runs that did not work.

TopRequester.description: A viewer and how many songs they have requested in this channel, all time.

viewerUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

TopViewer.description: A channel's top viewer over a range by the chosen metric (analytics.md §4) — not the economy board.

TopViewerMetric.description: The metric a top-viewers query ranks by (analytics.md §4).

fromViewerUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

toViewerUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

actorUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

TransferCommand.description: A point-to-point transfer between two viewers in the same channel (economy.md §4). long TransferCommand.Amount > 0.

TrustPolicy.description:
A channel's trust tuning as the dashboard sees it (S-OWN23). Carries VALUES only — every label and
plain-language explanation is frontend i18n, per the translations-never-in-code rule.
bool TrustPolicyDto.IsPinned is false while the channel is still tracking the shipped defaults, so the UI
can show "default" versus "you changed this" without guessing from the numbers.

detectionId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

broadcasterId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

confirmedByUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

overturnedByUserId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

TrustSafetyReviewItem.description:
One automatic account action the spam-defence engine took on its own (S-ADMIN-8a) — carries the
evidence that caused it and the current review state. string TrustSafetyReviewItemDto.ReversalPreview is the human-
readable blast radius of an overturn, computed before the operator commits to one.

TrustTierThresholds.description:
The per-channel thresholds an operator may tune (§L4.1: "thresholds are per-channel tunable; the
invariant is not"). Defaults are the spec's.

TtsConfig.description:
TTS configuration for a channel (tts.md P.1). BYOK keys never leave the server — only their
presence is surfaced, so the dashboard can show configured-state truthfully.
DefaultVoiceId is the EFFECTIVE voice (the channel's own pick, else the platform default
voice), so the page never shows a voice the runtime does not speak; FollowsPlatformDefaultVoice
says which of the two it is.

TtsConfigOptions.description:
What the TTS settings page may offer: the providers, dispatch modes and standings the update accepts, and
the longest message cap. Served from TtsConfigOptions, the same place the update validates against.

TtsDispatchOutcome.description: The result of a dispatch: what happened, plus the play URL when it was dispatched.

TtsHistoryEntry.description:
One spoken utterance in the channel's TTS history. Text is null for rows written before the
text was stored. Id is the row's cursor value. RequestedByName and
RequestedByColor come from the requester's user row, and are null when the bot has none.

TtsHistoryPage.description:
A newest-first page of the TTS history. NextBefore is the `before` value that fetches
the next older page, or null when this page reaches the oldest row.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

TtsLexiconEntry.description: One pronunciation-lexicon rule: when Phrase appears in an utterance, TTS speaks Replacement.

TtsOverlay.description:
The channel's auto-provisioned TTS overlay (widgets-overlays.md §1.2 system surface): the OBS browser-source
URL to add once, and when it last reported running (audit B5) — so the dashboard can show a real "is this
actually in OBS" signal instead of assuming.

id.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

TtsQueueEntry.description: A pending TTS utterance awaiting moderator review (tts.md P.1a), shaped for the moderator queue UI.

text.description: The line to speak. When null or blank, the server speaks the voice's own introduction.

TtsTestRequest.description: Request to test a TTS voice.

TtsTestResult.description: Result of a TTS test synthesis.

TtsVoice.description: An available TTS voice, with the catalogue metadata that powers search/filter and preview-before-pick.

username.description:
Twitch login of the viewer, only consulted when the import runs with `createMissing`: an unknown
Twitch user with a username is created as a bare viewer User (the chat-ingest get-or-create seam)
instead of being skipped. Optional — omitting it keeps the row skip-on-unknown.

TtsVoiceAssignmentRow.description: One row of a bulk per-viewer voice-assignment import: the Twitch user id and the catalogue voice they get.

TtsVoiceCandidate.description:
One voice the platform default may be set to: a catalogue voice every channel can speak without a key of
its own. IsDefault marks the current default.

TtsVoiceDefault.description:
The platform default TTS voice as the admin editor shows it: the catalogue voice every channel without its
own pick speaks with, how many channels follow it and how many picked their own.

TtsVoiceDefaultChange.description: A proposed platform default voice — the preview body.

TtsVoiceImportResult.description: The bulk-import outcome: how many assignments were upserted and every row that was skipped, with its reason.

TtsVoiceImportSkip.description: Why one import row was skipped instead of applied (`unknown_user` | `unknown_voice`).

TwitchAdSchedule.description:
The channel's ad schedule — next/last ad as unix seconds (0 when none), the current ad duration, the
remaining pre-roll-free time, and the snooze allowance (count plus the unix refresh time).

TwitchAdSnooze.description: Result of snoozing the next ad — the updated snooze count, refresh time, and pushed-back next-ad time (unix seconds).

TwitchAutoModSettings.description:
The channel's REAL Twitch AutoMod levels (0–4 per category, or one overall level driving them all).
Distinct from the bot's own `AutomodConfigDto` filters — this is Twitch's own pre-publish hold,
the only lever that stops a message before chat ever sees it.

TwitchClipStub.description:
The stub returned by a clip-create call (Create Clip, Create Clip From VOD): the new clip's id and the
edit URL the broadcaster opens to trim and publish it within the 15-second editing window.

TwitchCommercial.description: Result of starting a commercial — the length served, a status message, and the retry cooldown.

TwitchPoll.description: A poll the broadcaster created — its choices, voting settings, status and lifecycle timestamps.

TwitchPollChoice.description: One choice in a poll, with its running vote tallies (Get/Create/End Polls).

TwitchPredictionOutcome.description: One of the 2–10 possible outcomes of a prediction, with its running tally of predictors.

TwitchPredictionTopPredictor.description: A leading predictor on an outcome — points wagered and (once resolved) points won.

TwitchRaid.description: The pending raid created by Start a Raid — when it was created and whether the target is mature.

timezone.description:
The streamer's saved IANA timezone, stamped on by the API (Twitch does not return one). Null when the
streamer has not saved a zone; the dashboard then falls back to the device zone.

TwitchSchedule.description:
Get Channel Stream Schedule — the broadcaster's streaming schedule: the segment list, the active
vacation window (null when none), and the broadcaster's identity. The data is a single object, so the
transport's `data[]` envelope wraps exactly one of these.

TwitchScheduleCategory.description: The category (game) a schedule segment is tagged with.

timezone.description: The streamer's saved IANA timezone the segment is shown in; null when none is saved.

TwitchScheduleSegment.description: One broadcast segment in the schedule (a single or recurring entry).

TwitchScheduleVacation.description: The broadcaster's scheduled vacation window during which the schedule is suspended.

TwitchScopeDiagnostics.description:
The Twitch scope/connection health read model (twitch-helix.md §5): the connection status, the granted
scope set, and the per-feature requirement matrix the dashboard renders so a missing scope is observable
(it closes the "subscriber count always 0" / "403 chat" class of silent failures by surfacing the gap).

TwitchScopeRequirement.description:
One row of the diagnostics matrix: a scope a feature needs, whether the connection currently holds it, and
(because every entry here is a progressive, feature-gated scope) the feature that gates its request. A
missing progressive scope is "feature-gated", not an error — it is requested when the feature is enabled.

TwitchStreamMarker.description: The created marker returned by Create Stream Marker (its id, timestamp, offset and description).

UnbanRequest.description:
One unban request in the channel's queue, read live from Twitch — the requesting viewer, their
            appeal text, its status, and (once resolved) the moderator and resolution note.

UnbanUserRequest.description:
A dashboard unban request — the reversal of BanUserRequest. string UnbanUserRequest.Scope is
`"this_channel"` (default) or `"all_moderated"`, which lifts the ban across every channel Twitch says
the operator moderates (the "un-nuke").

UpdateBuiltinSettingsRequest.description: The channel's cooldown and permission floor for a built-in; null = use the default.

pipelineId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

UpdateCatalogItemRequest.description: Partial update of a catalog item (PATCH semantics — null = unchanged) (economy.md §4).

UpdateChannelAudioMixRequest.description:
MusicDuckPercent left out keeps the stored value, so a client that predates ducking
        never resets it.

prefix.description: The command prefix (1-5 non-whitespace chars, e.g. `!`). Null leaves it unchanged.

botLinePrefix.description:
The visible marker bot-emitted lines carry when the bot posts through the streamer's own account
(e.g. `*`, `#`, or an emoji; 1-4 chars). Empty string clears it back to none; null leaves
it unchanged.

locale.description: The channel's default language/locale (BCP-47, e.g. `en`). Null leaves it unchanged.

autoJoin.description: Whether the bot auto-joins this channel's chat. Null leaves it unchanged.

timezone.description: The streamer's IANA timezone (e.g. `Europe/Amsterdam`). Null leaves it unchanged.

keepActiveWhileOffline.description:
Whether commands and rewards stay active while the channel is offline (default off: they switch off when
the stream ends and back on when it starts). Null leaves it unchanged.

viewerCasualFrom.description:
The viewer message count from which `{user.activity.level}` reads `casual` (default 10). The three
steps must satisfy 1 <= casual < regular < veteran <= 1,000,000, checked together with the
stored values. Null leaves it unchanged.

viewerRegularFrom.description: The viewer message count from which the level reads `regular` (default 100). Null leaves it unchanged.

viewerVeteranFrom.description: The viewer message count from which the level reads `veteran` (default 500). Null leaves it unchanged.

UpdateChatColor.description: The new chat color: a Twitch color name (blue, hot_pink, ...) or a hex value like #9146FF.

UpdateChatFilterRequest.description: Patches an existing chat filter — only the supplied fields change.

oneOf.description: Where the template response goes and whether the overlay line is HTML. Absent leaves it unchanged.

pipelineId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

oneOf.description:
The new binding; absent leaves it unchanged. A pipeline target with no id (or an empty guid) clears it.
Wins over Guid? UpdateChatTriggerRequest.PipelineId.

minPermissionLevel.description: The rung name (see string CreateChatTriggerRequest.MinPermissionLevel); null leaves it.

name.description:
New trigger name; null leaves the existing name unchanged. Subject to the same
            prefix-stripping/uniqueness validation as creation.

minPermissionLevel.description: The rung name (see <see cref="!:CreateCommandRequest.MinPermissionLevel" />); null leaves it.

prefixMode.description: How the prefix is resolved: Default | Custom | None. Null leaves it unchanged.

customPrefix.description: Custom prefix when string? UpdateCommandDto.PrefixMode is Custom; empty string clears it.

matchMode.description: How the trigger input is matched: StartsWith | Exact | Contains | Regex. Null leaves it unchanged.

matchPattern.description: Regex pattern when string? UpdateCommandDto.MatchMode is Regex; empty string clears it.

pipelineId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

codeScriptId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

userCooldownSeconds.description: Per-user cooldown duration in seconds; 0 = off.

oneOf.description: Where the reply goes and whether the overlay line is HTML; omitted leaves the current setting.

UpdateCommand.description: Request to update an existing command.

pingRoleId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

UpdateEngagementConfigRequest.description: Update body for the engagement configuration (engagement.md §5).

pipelineId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

speakWithTts.description: A chat_message response also speaks its resolved text through the channel's TTS. Absent leaves it unchanged.

oneOf.description:
Where a chat_message response goes and whether the overlay line is HTML. Absent leaves it unchanged; a
delivery of plain Twitch chat is stored as the default.

What the response runs when its type is pipeline: a command (by id), a pipeline or an action. Wins
over Guid? UpdateEventResponseDto.PipelineId when both are sent; absent leaves the binding unchanged. The command
must exist in the channel.

UpdateEventResponse.description: Request to update an event response configuration.

verificationSecret.description: When present, rotates (re-encrypts) the verification secret.

targetPipelineId.description: Owned identifier — a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID (the API-boundary encoding of the server's UUIDv7 storage key). Accepted inbound as either this ULID or a raw GUID string.

UpdateMediaShareConfigRequest.description: Update body for the media-share config (media-share.md §5). A null EligibilityJson keeps the stored rules.

requestsOpen.description: Opens or closes new song requests; the music keeps playing and the queue stays.

maxSongSeconds.description: The longest song a viewer may request, in seconds. The broadcaster and moderators are not held to it.

allowExplicit.description: When false, a song the provider marks explicit is refused.

perStreamLimit.description:
The most songs one viewer may request in one stream, counting songs that already played. 0 turns the
cap off (null leaves the current value alone); a value of 1 to 100 turns it on.

youTubeMusicCategoryOnly.description:
When true, a YouTube upload must sit in the Music category or come from a "- Topic" artist channel.
When false, any on-demand video is admitted (fan uploads). A music.youtube.com link always counts.

minTrustLevel.description: Ignored. Who may request is set per source (`music:request:*`); kept so old clients still compile.

bangerPlaylistId.description: The playlist `!banger` adds to. Empty string clears the choice.

bangerAutoCreate.description: With no playlist chosen, `!banger` makes one on first use.

maxRequestsPerRole.description:
A song request cap per role (`viewer|subscriber|vip|moderator|broadcaster`, 1 to 50). A
requester gets the highest cap among the rungs they reach; a rung with no value uses

as the HttpOnly `nnz_refresh_token` cookie on the calling origin.

WidgetDetail.description:
A widget's full detail. The authored source and compiled bundle are NOT here — they live on append-only
`WidgetVersion` rows; Guid? WidgetDetail.ActiveVersionId names the version the overlay currently serves.
`Framework` is the source language (vue|vanilla; react and svelte are refused); `Source` is the provenance
(first_party|verified_gallery|custom). bool WidgetDetail.GalleryUpdateAvailable is true when
Guid? WidgetDetail.GalleryItemId is set and the gallery item's source has moved on since this widget was installed
or last updated from it — the streamer's clone is running stale code. Always false for a self-authored
`custom` widget (no gallery link to compare against). bool WidgetDetail.IsAttached is true when a live
browser source has this widget open right now (`IOverlayPresenceRegistry`) — the "overlay last-seen"
signal, so a streamer can tell an overlay is actually loaded in OBS without firing a test event.
bool WidgetDetail.IsCustomized is true when the channel has saved its own code over a catalogue widget's source
(a first-party system widget or a gallery install) — the dashboard marks it "Edited" and offers the reset to
the catalogue source; a catalogue update never overwrites it on its own. Always false for a `custom`
widget, which has no catalogue source to differ from.

WidgetPreviewActionRequest.description: A preview action request: the action type, its parameters and the variables that seed its context.

WidgetPreviewActionResponse.description: What the preview action did; the same fields the overlay hub's invoke returns.

WidgetSettingsField.description:
One editable setting on a widget. string WidgetSettingsField.Type picks the control the dashboard renders:
`bool` (switch), `number` (stepper/slider), `text` (field), `color` (colour control),
`select` (single-choice dropdown over IReadOnlyList<WidgetSettingsFieldOption>? WidgetSettingsField.Options), `multiselect` (chip toggles over
IReadOnlyList<WidgetSettingsFieldOption>? WidgetSettingsField.Options), or `json` (raw-JSON textarea for a structural map/list the schema does not flatten).
object? WidgetSettingsField.Default is the catalogue default (so a cleared field falls back to the widget's shipped value);
double? WidgetSettingsField.Min/double? WidgetSettingsField.Max/double? WidgetSettingsField.Step bound a numeric control; LocalizedText WidgetSettingsField.Group lets the form
section the fields. string? WidgetSettingsField.Picker (a `text` field only) names a pipeline resource-picker kind
(`twitch_reward`, `obs_audio_input`, …): the form then offers a searchable list instead of a typed box,
and the saved value is that kind's option value. LocalizedText WidgetSettingsField.Label, LocalizedText? WidgetSettingsField.Help, and LocalizedText WidgetSettingsField.Group are all
LocalizedText (S-SCHEMA-I18N-redesign) — a translation KEY only; the dashboard resolves each
against `strings.xml` for the viewer's locale instead of the backend serving a hardcoded English literal.

WidgetSettingsFieldOption.description:
A single choice for a `select`/`multiselect` field: the wire string WidgetSettingsFieldOption.Value (the machine value
stored/compared, never shown) and its display LocalizedText WidgetSettingsFieldOption.Label — a LocalizedText
(S-SCHEMA-I18N-redesign) translation KEY only, resolved by the dashboard against `strings.xml`.

WidgetSettingsSchema.description:
The typed settings schema for one first-party widget type (widgets-overlays.md). It is the contract the
dashboard renders a generic, schema-driven settings form from — so a first-party widget is configured through
controls, never by hand-editing its Vue source. Derived from the widget's authored `cfg` shape and its
catalogue `DefaultSettings`; every settings key the widget honours is covered by exactly one
WidgetSettingsField (a coverage test fails the build if a type drifts un-schematised).
IReadOnlyList<string> WidgetSettingsSchema.EventSubscriptions is the widget's default wire topics — read-only reference (the widget's data
wiring is intrinsic, not user-config), shown so the operator sees what the overlay listens for.

WidgetTemplate.description:
A starter widget template the editor offers when creating a new custom widget — a working, SDK-using starting
point (never a blank editor). string WidgetTemplate.Source is the authored source to seed into the editor + compile.

WidgetTestEventRequest.description: The test-fire request: an event type, and an optional explicit payload (a sample is used when omitted).

WidgetTestEventResult.description:
What a test fire did for the one overlay it targeted: whether the overlay reacts to the event (so it
    was sent), and whether a browser source had it open to play it.

OBS before the old one stops working, instead of the source going blank with no warning.
